description.value:
Cryptidkin. Normalized Bad Eden ancestry root.

Select one subspecies when building the character: Chupacabra, Jackalope, Furrykin.

This root grants the shared Cryptidkin core trait package. Subspecies layer flavor, size, and Tier powers on top.

“Every settlement has a story about you. None of them are accurate. All of them are useful.”

Cryptidkin Core Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid (Cryptidkin).

  • Size. Small or Medium (set by subspecies).

  • Speed. 6 squares (subspecies may override).

  • attributes. Your background determines your attribute increases; Cryptidkin does not grant fixed bonuses. Subspecies lean expressed through Tier powers.

Folklore Presence. When you first encounter an NPC group, the GM chooses (or rolls) whether you are met as omen, trophy, or legend. It is never neutral. People have heard of your kind. They are almost always wrong, and that is almost always useful.

Wasteland Adapted. You reroll the lowest die on checks against disease and environmental poison. You ignore the first nonmagical environmental hazard you encounter each Strategic Turn (heat, cold, radiation taint, wind shear, fume pockets).

Survivor’s Instinct. When you roll initiative, you can choose to know the position of the nearest exit, the nearest threat, or the nearest ally within 12 squares You cannot be surprised while conscious.

Subspecies. Choose one Cryptidkin subspecies (Chupacabra, Jackalope, Furrykin). Your subspecies grants Tier powers as you level (Tier I at creation, then 5/11/17).

Cryptidkin Subspecies. This heritage preserves the original UUID for Jackalope (Bad Eden) while converting it from a species-root to a Cryptidkin subspecies.

“You don’t spot a Jackalope. You notice the world flinch, and then realize why.”

Jackalope. Fast because they have to be. Twitchy because the world has trained them that stillness is how you die. Half-remembered pre-Shattering folklore, half radiation-assembled rumor, and fully people.

Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid (Cryptidkin).

  • Size. Small or Medium.

  • Speed. 7 squares

  • Subspecies Lean. Your subspecies leans toward INTR (Intrigue)—expressed through Tier powers.

Core: Folklore & Frame

At creation you gain Folklore & Frame (Folklore Presence, Wasteland Adapted, Survivor’s Instinct).

Jackalope Tier Powers

You gain Tier I at creation, then Tier II (5), Tier III (11), Tier IV (17). Jackalope powers emphasize: Startle Reflex (can’t-be-caught-flat burst), Wasteland Bound (long-distance run), Horns of Bad Luck (jinx aura), Can’t Catch Me (evasion), and strategic Bad Omen Runner faction hooks.

Strategic Hooks (Foundry / Bad Eden)

If you see Jackalope tracks circling your hex, you are not under attack. You are being advised.

  • OP Edge. Your faction gains +1 Soft Power OP and +1 Non-Lethal OP at campaign start.

  • Trail Whisper. Once per Strategic Turn, your faction can reroll a single Travel or Scout check made in a hex adjacent to your home territory.

"You aren't fast because you're fast. You're fast because the world keeps deciding to miss."

Startle Reflex (1/Soma Break). Reaction when you are targeted by an attack roll or fail an Intrigue check — move up to 2 squares without provoking opportunity attacks.

Horns of Bad Luck. Your natural horns ship as a Jackalope-only Manifestation when you take the heritage — see your Manifestations tab. When violence escalates around you, the GM may describe unsettling omens tied to your presence — a mirror crack, a dropped knife, a candle going out the wrong direction.

“Magic is grammar. Reality is a draft.”

You are a prepared, academic manifestant who edits meaning directly. You do not delegate power; you channel it raw.

Esoteric OS Integration: Your manifesting interacts with correspondences (school ↔ sephirah, day/slot timing). Alignment yields Resonance; misalignment accumulates Strain.

Curated List (doc-only): Cosmic Linguists favor semantic leverage, control, ritual work, and correspondence-aligned craft.

Resonance Dice (shared pool): You gain Resonance when you cast in correspondence-aligned timing or complete proper ritual work. You may spend Resonance to increase potency (see Resonance Channel).

Strain (shared meter): You gain Strain when you cast misaligned, overcharge effects, or force semantic contradictions. At thresholds, the GM triggers Backlash: reality glitches, psychic recoil, or narrative consequences.

Wizards get to be powerful. Wizards also pay the bill.

🔮 CLASS RESOURCE: Resonance

Type: Dice-based resource pool
Purpose: Measures alignment with reality’s underlying structure

Resonance Dice

  • Start as d6

  • Increase at:

    • Level 5 → d8

    • Level 11 → d10

    • Level 17 → d12

  • Maximum stored dice:
    = your Mind modifier (minimum 1)

Gaining Resonance

You gain 1 Resonance Die when:

  • You cast a manifestation in correct esoteric alignment

  • You complete a properly prepared ritual

  • You exploit an established semantic pattern

  • Your subclass leverages symbolism, structure, or constraint

Limit:
You may gain only 1 Resonance Die per round.

Resonance decays quickly — it is momentum, not savings.

Spending Resonance

When you spend a Resonance Die, roll it and apply one effect:

  • Add the result to a Resolve DC

  • Add an extra damage or effect die

  • Extend duration or scope

  • Impose roll 3d10 keep lowest 2 on a defense checks

  • Stabilize a manifestation against countering

Each die spent may generate Strain.

⚠ PUSHBACK SYSTEM: Strain

Type: Escalating consequence meter
Purpose: Measures damage to reality from forced edits

Gaining Strain

You gain +1 Strain when:

  • Casting while misaligned

  • Spending Resonance aggressively

  • Forcing contradictory meanings

  • Using certain subclass features

Some abilities add Strain automatically.

Strain Thresholds (Recommended)

  • 1–2: Cosmetic anomalies, sensory bleed

  • 3–4: Psychic damage, manifestation distortion

  • 5–6: Reality glitches, hostile manifestations

  • 7+: GM-controlled backlash

Clearing Strain

  • Rest

  • Downtime

  • Careful ritual casting

  • Annotator features

  • Pactkeeper intervention

Strain is dangerous but manageable.

🧠 SUMMARY FOR PLAYERS

  • Pactkeepers manage authority

  • Cosmic Linguists manage momentum

  • Jurisdiction = what you are allowed to touch

  • Civic Charge = permission you spend

  • Precedent = what now matters

  • Resonance = how hard you push

  • Strain = what it costs

Nothing here is vague.
Nothing here is hand-wavy.
Everything can be adjudicated at the table consistently.

Spend 1 Resonance Die and open the Resonance Channel dialog.

  • +1 Resolve DC

  • Add one additional damage/effect die

  • Extend duration one step

  • Impose roll 3d10 keep lowest 2 on one save

  • Stabilize against counters / dispels

⟁ Per-Use Ability — Resonance Channel (Spend) Recovery: 1/round (gain)  ·  Action: Free (with manifestation)  ·  Use: Click this feature on your sheet to invoke. Spend 1 Resonance Die and pick one channel: +1 Resolve DC · add an extra damage/effect die · extend duration one step · impose roll 3d10 keep lowest 2 on one defense · stabilize against counter/dispel.

“I am not casting. I am editing.”

Choose an Editing Mode: Additive, Subtractive, Transformative, Referential, or Performative. Your mode shapes how your manifestations manifest, what they cost in Strain, and what Backlash looks like.

This is semantic authority, not damage scaling.
Strain tracks symbolic overload, semantic contradiction, and magical backlash caused by pushing language too hard.

When you spend Clarity to manifest, you may name the target as part of the action. For the rest of the scene, extending that manifestation's Reach to the named target costs 1 less Surge / Blood Debt (minimum 0).

description.value:
"Say what counts as what now. Reality is listening."

Doctrine: Reality bends when likeness is declared and believed — your workings hinge on symbolic equivalence.

The Metaphor Apostle rules by declaration. Your Surge spends rewrite what things are: an ally becomes a wall, a foe's armor becomes paper, and your whole line becomes giants.

Doctrine (spent via Surge)

  • Declared Likeness (1) — "you are a wall": an ally gains DR equal to Tier.
  • Declared Frailty (2) — "their armor is paper": a foe's next attack and its saves are at disadvantage.
  • Apotheosis (5) — "you are all giants": allies within 6 squares gain DR equal to Tier and a reroll.

"Strike the clause. Insert your own. Reality reads from the top."

The Cosmic Linguist edits reality like text — meaning first, matter second. One currency now: Surge. The editor always has the next word, so you bank +1 Surge at the start of your turn (the old Resonance, Strain, and Editorial Authority pools are folded into this single pool).

The Edit (spent via Surge)

  • Emphasis (1) — your next Strike or manifestation hits for +Tier d6 (the word, underlined).
  • Stabilize (2) — you gain DR equal to Tier; your next cast resists counter / dispel (the sentence holds).
  • Impose a Reading (3) — a foe's next attack and its saves are at disadvantage (only one correct interpretation: yours).
  • Rewrite the Sentence (5) — a foe loses its reactions and rolls saves at disadvantage; allies near you bank a reroll.

The Sentence endures as your signature stance — while held, the manifestation's primary target is bound by name and rolls its checks against you at disadvantage.

"You are not an animal that learned to talk. You are a story the world made into a person because it needed you in the room."

If yes, reroll the lowest die on your first Diplomacy (Presence) or Intimidation (Presence) check with anyone in that community (your choice which skill, declared when you roll). The rumor is not always flattering — the GM gets to colour it.

Survivor's Instinct. 1/Soma Break, when you would drop to 0 Integrity, you may instead drop to 1 Integrity and gain one level of Stress.

Archetype Effects

  • Tier Engine. See this Archetype’s Tier feats (Tier 1–4) for the full tactical and strategic expression of scholarship, arcane literacy, research throughput, and recovered knowledge.

description.value:
Crew Type (Bad Eden): Covert Ops Cell.

“If you saw it happen, it wasn’t us.”

Covert Ops cells make wars quiet. They prefer locks to speeches, shadows to banners, and results to credit. They don’t start fights—they rearrange the board so the fight never happens.

  • Tactical Identity: You gain a skill rank in Stealth and with the Tinkering aptitude.
  • Strategic Identity: Your faction starts with +1 Intrigue OPs.

Splendor - Meaning made visible. +1 Intrigue, +1 Diplomacy OPs

Hod renders truth through language, symbol, and presentation. It rewards courtly play, ritual precision, and the ability to turn naming, framing, and interpretation into strategic force.

Occult Association (Bad Eden): Kabbalist.

“The map is not the territory. The territory is also not the territory.”

Kabbalists are not wizards. They are cartographers of meaning — the kind who draw a line and the world decides it has always been there.

They study the Tree the way an engineer studies a bridge: load, strain, failure points, and where the pressure is going when nobody is looking. Sephiroth is flow. Qliphoth is leak. And if you learn the geometry well enough, you can reroute the flood before it drowns the region.

To a Kabbalist, the Great Work is not aspiration. It is alignment. Name the thing correctly, place it correctly, and reality stops wasting energy pretending to be something else.

How Kabbalists pursue the Great Work:

  • By reading Hexes like paragraphs — sephirothic intent, qliphothic rot, and the lies in-between
  • By reducing the cost of identifying Sparks and metaphysical conditions
  • By treating the Tree as infrastructure rather than metaphor
  • By shifting alignment deliberately, even when the world pushes back

Resonance: Tree / Binah-Tiferet axis — structure, pattern-recognition, and the disciplined naming of what is actually happening.

Tell-tales: finger-traced grids, muttered node-names, diagrams drawn over maps that somehow make the maps more true.

Faction Effect (Passive):

  • +1 to Soft Power OP rolls

Cost Principle: Kabbalistic order clarifies, but clarification creates strain. When you force alignment, hidden contradictions surface somewhere else.

Tier 1 (Level 1) — The Magician

  • Tactical: You gain a skill rank in Occult and Lore. You learn one Tier-0 manifestation from the Wizard manifestation list.
  • Strategic: Your faction's passive OP bias now follows the base Archetype file.

Tier 1 — Covert Ops Cell

“If you saw it happen, it wasn’t us.”

Covert Ops cells make wars quiet. They prefer locks to speeches, shadows to banners, and results to credit. They don’t start fights—they rearrange the board so the fight never happens.

You’re learning the shape of your shadow. Expect mistakes. Budget for them.

  • Tactical: You gain a skill rank in Stealth and with the Tinkering aptitude.
  • Strategic: Your faction starts with +1 Intrigue OPs.

Tier 1 — Kabbalist

“The map is not the territory. The territory is also not the territory.”

At Tier 1, you have learned to see what other people are walking through. The Tree leaves fingerprints on everything. You have merely trained yourself to stop ignoring them.

Tactical (Character Scale)

  • Gain a skill rank in Faith. If you already have it, take another GM-approved skill proficiency.
  • Sense the Leak: you can cast Detect Evil and Good 1/Soma Break, flavored as sensing sephirothic flow and qliphothic pressure.

Strategic (Faction Scale)

  • Hex Read: upon entering a new Hex, you immediately learn its dominant Sephirothic or Qliphothic alignment, if any.
  • Soft Power Precision: your faction’s Soft Power OP rolls gain +3.

Cost: perception is not neutral. Once you can see the leak, you stop being able to ignore it. Expect strain, attention, or moral pressure when you name what others would rather leave vague.

⟁ Per-Use Ability — Sense the Leak
Recovery: 1/Soma Break  ·  Action: Action  ·  Use: Click this feature on your sheet to invoke.

You conjure a scene-long metaphor entity.

Effect: Create an allegorical manifestation (Judge, Mirror, Choir, Hungry Crown). It provides control, distraction, and leverage without direct damage (GM adjudication).

Spark Sense

Some truths are louder than sound.

Rules

You gain a skill rank in Occult (Mind). If you already have it, you gain mastery.

As an action, you may focus on the unseen and learn one of the following about a creature, object, or place within 6 squares (choose one):

  • Whether it is suffused with magic-like resonance
  • Whether it feels aligned toward Renewal or toward Corruption (GM adjudication)
  • Whether it bears an active ward, curse, or binding

You can use this principle a number of times equal to your skill rank bonus, regaining all uses on a Sanctuary.

(3rd Level)

You establish a symbolic hook in the scene.

Declare a symbol (sigil, phrase, icon, prop).

For the rest of the scene:

  • Manifestations referencing that symbol may gain additional Resonance.

  • Influence may extend further when narratively aligned.

Hooks reward continuity.

Symbols want to propagate.

(3rd Level)

You anchor manifestations to declared metaphors.

When you cast illusion or enchantment, you may declare a symbolic anchor:

  • Crown

  • Chain

  • Mirror

  • Storm

  • Fire

  • Mask

  • Hunt

  • Etc.

If the metaphor is meaningfully relevant in the scene:

  • Gain Resonance.

If the metaphor is contradicted:

  • Immediately gain Strain.

This is not flavor.

The metaphor must be maintained.

Battlefield Presence

People fight better when you are near.

Rules

Allies within 2 squares of you reroll the lowest die on the first defense checks they make against being Shaken or charmed each combat.

Initiation 6 — Translation. 1/scene signature move: as a reaction to an ally completing a manifestation within Reach, transcribe it into your idiom. Until the end of the next round, you carry their effect at your tier cap (clamped to Manifestation Ruleset v1.0 footprint), paying its upkeep from your Clarity. Your translation, your bill.

Discipline: passive Reach discount unchanged from Init 1; Translation itself is a 1/scene narrative power resolved at the table.

⟁ Per-Use Ability — Translation Recovery: 1/scene  ·  Action: Reaction  ·  Use: Click this feature on your sheet to invoke. When an ally completes a manifestation within Reach, transcribe it into your idiom. Carry their effect at your tier cap until end of next round; pay upkeep from your Clarity.

(6th Level)

You bind behavior to story roles.

Choose an archetype:

  • The Betrayer

  • The Tyrant

  • The Martyr

  • The Fool

  • The Guardian

  • The Tempter

The target must play the role:

  • Hesitate

  • Monologue

  • Retreat

  • Confess

  • Overreach

  • Submit to a constraint

Cost

Generates Strain if forced aggressively.

Clarification

This does not override free will.
It constrains choices within archetypal gravity.

The more resistant the target, the greater the Strain risk.

description.value:
Calm the Mob

Crowds don’t think. They feel. So you give them something else to feel.

Rules

You gain a skill rank in Diplomacy (Presence) or Intimidation (Presence) (your choice). If you already have it, you gain mastery.

When you spend at least 1 minute addressing a group of non-hostile or uncertain creatures, you may make a Presence (Diplomacy (Presence) or Intimidation (Presence)) check (DC set by the GM). On a success, you reduce immediate hostility: the crowd hesitates, disperses, or agrees to hear terms. On a failure, you still buy time, but a complication occurs (a challenger steps forward, guards arrive, a rumor spreads).

(10th Level)

You cast across groups through shared symbolism.

Choose a collective identity:

  • Crowd

  • Mob

  • Choir

  • Army

  • Congregation

  • Survivors

You may affect the group as a unified symbolic system:

  • Shared illusion

  • Shared fear

  • Shared calm

  • Shared belief

It feels like fate—not domination.

Resonance Interaction

Group alignment can generate additional Resonance.

Risk

If the shared metaphor fractures, Strain spikes.

Initiation 11 — The Sentence (Signature Mode). Stance. While The Sentence is held, every manifestation you sustain treats its primary target as bound by name — mechanical hook for holds, binds, and compelled-truth at the GM's table. Pays ongoing upkeep against your Clarity.

Discipline (mode clSentence): while ON, additional Reach discount −1 (stacks with Init 1 for a total of −2 on Blood-Debt-reach). Click this feature on the sheet to toggle the stance.

Pilot: lock exact upkeep curve and break condition after one playtest cycle.

⟁ Per-Use Ability — The Sentence Recovery: Stance (signature)  ·  Action: Action (open / drop)  ·  Use: Click this feature on your sheet to invoke. Hold to bind primary targets of sustained manifestations by name (mechanical hook for holds, binds, compelled-truth). Pays ongoing upkeep against Clarity.

Leyline Attunement

You don’t just cross the world. You listen to it.

Rules

When you take a Respite, you may attune to the local flow. Until your next Sanctuary, you gain one of the following benefits (choose when you attune):

  • Guidance of the Current: You reroll the lowest die on one Athletics (Violence) checks you make each hour of travel.
  • Quiet Step: You reroll the lowest die on one Stealth (Intrigue) checks you make each hour of travel.
  • Resonant Warning: You reroll the lowest die on Initiative (Intrigue) rolls made in the first combat after you begin travel.

You can change the chosen benefit each time you attune.

Medic of the Wastes

Out here, healing is logistics.

Rules

You gain a skill rank in Faith (Soul). If you already have it, you gain mastery.

When you use a medkit to stabilize a creature, it also regains Integrity equal to your skill rank bonus.

Additionally, during a Respite, you may allow up to two creatures to regain additional Integrity equal to your skill rank bonus. A creature can benefit from this principle only once per Respite.

description.value:
Initiation 16 — Word That Was. 1/Soma Break, retroactively re-narrate one of your misfires as if the manifestation had succeeded at one tier lower than the one you spent for. Pay the lower tier's base upkeep instead. Where others spent the syllables and lost the meaning, you spent the meaning and chose the syllables.

Click this feature on the sheet to mark spent and post the chat card. Reset on Soma Break.

⟁ Per-Use Ability — Word That Was
Recovery: 1/Soma Break  ·  Action: Reaction (after misfire)  ·  Use: Click this feature on your sheet to invoke.
Re-narrate one of your misfires as if the manifestation had succeeded one tier lower than the tier you spent for. Pay the lower tier's base upkeep.

Refuse the Narrative

No. That is not how this ends.

Rules

Once per Soma Break, after rolling but before the result is resolved, you may treat a roll of 9 or lower on a 2d10x10 as a 10.

(18th Level)

You force metaphor into literal reality.

Once per arc:

Declare a metaphor.

For the scene, it becomes physically true.

Examples:

  • “He is a storm.” → Environmental upheaval follows him.

  • “This place is a cage.” → Exits resist escape.

  • “They are wolves.” → Pack coordination manifests.

  • “This city is a wound.” → Bleeding consequences escalate.

Cost

Catastrophic Strain.

Backlash is guaranteed.

Reality will respond after the scene.

You cannot Make It True quietly.

The universe remembers.

Enduring Focus

You hold your will together when others lose it.

Rules

You reroll the lowest die on Body checks made to maintain Clarity hold. Additionally, you can perform somatic components even when holding weapons or a shield.

item.lore:
A laminated paper coupon. Two for one breakfast taquitos, valid through a date so old the typeface itself is illegal in three coalitions. Yes. People will trade you a horse for it. Yes, even now. Yes, I'm aware that doesn't make sense. Take it up with the Akashic field.

Currency of the Frontier-Formerly-Known. Once per session, in any wasteland market or trading post, this coupon counts as a Tier-II trade good for purposes of barter. After the trade, it goes back in your pocket. The vendor is still happy about it three days later.

description.value:
You're not sure when it started. You found one in your jacket after a fight you survived. Then another after a deal you regretted. Then another after a kindness you forgot you'd done. The receipts are itemized, dated, and printed in a font that doesn't quite exist. They are addressed to you. They are sometimes harsh. They are never wrong.

The Ledger Knows. Soulbound to you the moment you accept the first receipt. Once per session, present a recent receipt to a Pactkeeper, an archivist, or a sufficiently old institutional NPC. They treat the receipt as legitimate testimony. (Mal: "Yes. They will. I don't know why. Don't ask. Just use it sparingly.")

item.signature: An itemized receipt appears in your pocket every time you witness something significant. They are usually unflattering.

manifestation.gmCalibration: Tier I bound natural weapon — never escalates without explicit player cost.

description.value:
"You aren't sure when you grew them. They were waiting for you when you stopped pretending."

Natural Attack. Bonus action — make a melee unarmed strike with your horns. Deals 1d6 kinetic damage (piercing flavor) on a hit.

Bad-Luck Omens. When violence escalates around you, the GM may describe unsettling omens tied to your presence — a mirror crack, a dropped knife, a candle going out the wrong direction.

Manifestation (Tier I, soulbound). These horns are part of you. They cannot be sundered, lost, or stolen — they vanish on your death and reappear on the next Jackalope to inherit the bloodline's luck.

system.effect: Target: Soul defense vs Cast DC. On fail: Staggered (movement halved, −2 attacks) and Guard −2 for 1 round.
system.flavor: There aren't any clowns. You can tell because they aren't here. That isn't helping.

manifestation.concept: Mal whispers and the target sees four greasepainted gentlemen they cannot quite focus on. They are honking. They are also, somehow, behind.

system.effect: Target: Body defense vs Cast DC. On fail: Prone for 1 round.
system.flavor: It's still there. They just don't believe in it for a moment.

manifestation.concept: Mal points out that the floor is, technically, a story everyone agreed to. The target loses the thread of that story.

system.effect: Force a reroll of the last attack, save, damage or ability check made by anyone within range.
system.flavor: With a subtle zoop, reality backspaces one keystroke.

manifestation.concept: Retract the roll that occurred immediately prior and force a reroll
Edit the target's most recent memories to something distracting, causing them to lose focus on their current activity.

system.flavor: He drew a line through what he had just said. They forgot. He did not.

manifestation.concept: You delete a recent sentence — a thing said, a thing acted, a thing recorded — from the canon of the scene. It happened. It is no longer the case that it happened.
manifestation.durationText: Permanent — until someone else writes the moment back in.
manifestation.riskText: Major edits draw attention from other Linguists, archivists, and any reality-stable witness (some saints, some children, some Pactkeepers).
manifestation.pathResonance: Cosmic Linguist (Redactor) — power lies in clean omission.
manifestation.fictionalPermission: You can take back a word that has already been said. Reality cooperates. Mostly.
manifestation.gmCalibration: T2 Working. Cannot delete events that constitute the spine of the scene. GM may require a higher tier for that.
manifestation.mechanicalHook: Erase one specific action, statement, or observation from the last 60 seconds. People in the scene revise their memory. Hard evidence (writing, recording) develops a flaw or smudge.
manifestation.signature: The deleted moment leaves a thin line through the air, a visible strikethrough that fades over the next minute.
manifestation.thirdThing: The deleted moment still happened in the deleter's memory. You will remember it forever, even if no one else does.

system.flavor: Mal: 'Yes, of course it's the Sephirah of glamour. What else would it be.'
